questions.prompt: Why does fleet let the router pass results between experts instead of letting one expert call another?
options: Each expert stays inside its own limits, and the router can log every step
pi forbids an expert from using tools
questions.explanation: If an expert called another, its guards would cover another expert's work. With a router handoff each expert answers only its part.

questions.prompt: In chain.ts the quant task contains {previous}. What happens before the quant expert sees it?
options: The text is sent as it is
The code replaces {previous} with the SQL expert's result
The quant expert is asked to fetch the SQL result itself
The router deletes the placeholder and sends nothing
questions.explanation: The loop replaces {previous} with the last result, so the quant expert reads one task that holds the data.

questions.prompt: Why does chain.ts stop a chain at 3 steps?
options: pi cannot run more than 3 prompts
Each step costs tokens and can drift, so a limit keeps the cost known
The log file holds only 3 lines
questions.explanation: A chain can grow without end, and every step adds cost. A hard cap keeps the cost bounded.
